text:
ryan: :rotating_light: infra-bot alerted about repeated GPU attach failures in ap-southeast1, looks tied to local NVMe write errors. creating thread to coordinate.
infra-bot: [ALERT] local-nvme write_errors > 5% on nodes pool=ephemeral-ap-southeast1 (last 10m). probe-id=nvme-write-4987
maya: any logs? which job types are hitting this? batch vs interactive?
ryan: mostly batch GPU jobs (large seq length). quick sample from one affected node:
```
[12345.678901] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 98765432
[12345.678912] nvme: write timeout, sqid 1 cid 128
[12347.000001] overlayfs: upperdir corruption detected, writeback failed
[12347.000100] kernel: task kworker/1:2 blocked for more than 120 seconds
```
jonas: hmm overlayfs writeback failures + nvme timeouts -> possible thermal throttle or writeback storm. metrics show a sharp fs_trim and scrub overlap at 04:00 UTC.
maya: confirmed: fstrim-cron and janitor-scrub both run in the same midnight window for this pool. iops spikes line up with the failures.
dina: GPU provisioning queue spiked ~2.5x and retries are increasing costs. customers hitting capacity fallback. we should mitigate asap, even if temporary.
ryan: proposed immediate mitigations:
- throttle janitor scrubs on ephemeral-ap-southeast1 (reduce parallelism)
- reschedule fstrim to off-peak and stagger with scrubs
- lower vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs and increase writeback threads priority
- failover new GPU attach requests to eu-west1 for the next 2h
ops-oncall: i can run the throttle change now. command to reduce scrub parallelism (run on janitor controller):
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/janitor-config -p '{"data": {"scrub_parallelism": "2"}}'
```
and to pause fstrim on pool nodes (temporary):
```
ssh node-XXXX
sudo systemctl stop fstrim.timer
```
jonas: also recommend toggling kernel param on a 2-node canary before fleet-wide change:
```
sudo sysctl -w vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs=150
```
maya: i'll watch dmesg+nvme SMART on the canary and alert in 15m.
ops-oncall: running the configmap patch now, applying scrub_parallelism=2 -> rolling restart of janitor controllers starting.
ryan: routing policy: added a temporary rule to route new GPU allocs from ap-southeast1 to eu-west1 (next 2h) — changed in smart-routing:policy=region-fallback.
dina: thanks. i'll notify capacity/sales to expect brief regional shift and cost bump for retries.
jonas: created ticket INC-2026 (ephemeral-ap-southeast1 nvme writeback storms) with initial triage and mitigation steps.
maya: canary node logs after sysctl change: no further blk_update_request in last 10m, nvme temps dropped ~4C. good signal but need sustained run.
ryan: plan for the rest of the day:
- keep scrub parallelism=2 and paused fstrim for 2h
- monitor nvme write_errors, gpu-provision-fail, attach-retries dashboards
- if stable after 2h, stagger fstrim at +6h and incrementally raise scrub parallelism
- follow-up postmortem if we see any persistent overlay corruption
ops-oncall: i've left notes in the runbook and will roll back patch if other pools are impacted.
ryan: big thanks. follow-up sync at 0900 UTC if still open. assigning owners: ops-oncall -> mitigation, jonas -> ticket, maya -> canary monitoring, dina -> customer comms. :thumbsup:
